blocks.text: Categories to Keep Out of Git

rows: .env, API keys, private keys (id_rsa, *.pem), service account JSON, database passwords
Commit .env.example with placeholder values; use a secret manager and CI secrets (Module 6)
Commit lock files (package-lock.json, poetry.lock) and install in CI
Rebuild in CI; publish release artifacts separately
Videos, datasets, design files, ML model weights
Git LFS, object storage, or a dataset registry
Logs, SQLite dev databases, coverage reports, caches
Production DB dumps, exports containing emails or addresses

blocks.text: Do commit lock files. They pin exact dependency versions so every developer and every CI run installs the same thing. Ignoring package-lock.json or poetry.lock is a common mistake that causes "works on my machine" bugs.
Why Secrets Are the Worst Case

items: History is permanent: removing a secret in a new commit leaves it readable in every previous commit and in every clone.
Public repositories are scanned continuously by automated bots; leaked cloud keys are often abused within minutes.
Forks and clones you do not control already have a copy, so rewriting history cannot guarantee removal.
Private repositories are not safe either: access changes, repositories get made public, laptops get stolen.
Revoke or rotate the credential immediately. This is the only step that actually neutralizes the leak; treat the secret as compromised.
Check provider logs for any use of the leaked credential.
Remove it from history with git filter-repo (Module 4) and force push, coordinating with the team since everyone must re-clone or reset.
If the repository is on GitHub, contact GitHub Support to purge cached views of the sensitive data if needed.
Add the file pattern to .gitignore and a scanning tool to prevent recurrence.

blocks.text: Rewriting history without rotating the secret is not a fix. Rotating the secret without rewriting history is an acceptable fix. The order matters: rotate first.

blocks.code:
# .env.example (committed): documents required variables, no real values
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/inventory
STRIPE_API_KEY=sk_test_replace_me
JWT_SECRET=change-me

# .env (ignored): real values, never committed

items: Add .env and key file patterns to .gitignore before writing the first secret.
Run a secret scanner as a pre-commit hook, for example gitleaks or detect-secrets, so leaks are caught before they enter history.
Enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection, which blocks pushes that contain known secret formats.
Review git diff --staged before every commit; it is your last manual checkpoint.

blocks.code:
# .pre-commit-config.yaml (pre-commit framework)
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks
    rev: v8.18.4
    hooks:
      - id: gitleaks
